articles.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors. Recently, she paused her travels to accept the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award — and to share how she finds the right people and companies to imagine and produce at massive scale technology that has never been built before. Foxconn Q: How would you describe your job to someone outside NVIDIA? A: At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain. A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before. If you don’t have all three, you can’t create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner. Q: What’s an example of that in practice ? A: Amphenol’s cable cartridge is the most complex interconnect assembly they have ever built. When I recently visited the Vietnam factory, now in full production, I was struck by the level of precision required to build a product of this complexity. In this large cable cartridge, there are 1,500 small cable legs. Each one requires a very precise assembly to yield a quality level of less than 1 DPPM, or defect part per million. Amphenol built over a hundred automated lines to produce this product at the speed and scale we require. That takes know-how and technology, but it also takes heart, willingness and dedication. Creating anything of that complexity and precision with a supplier forges the partnership. The partners NVIDIA maintains are the ones who supported us when we were small, and yet are willing to scale with us today. Q: What changed as NVIDIA went from selling chips to building systems and platforms? A: When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned. As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we’ve also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing. For example, our optical component partners have the technology and the willingness, but they don’t yet have the scale or capital to build fabs for the volume we need. To grow, we needed to support and invest, like we did with Coherent and Lumentum . Beyond that, with products like CPO (co-packaged optics), we’re creating entirely new supply chains with scale partners that are new to the optics world. articles.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”   Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26   In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. It also uses 4x fewer lasers, which means fewer components that can fail. Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s. Liquid cooling carries heat away from the switch chip and optical engines. The company reports a median optics temperature of 36°C, compared with 51°C for conventional pluggable optics, and its tests find more stable signal integrity. NVIDIA Photonics also brings the electrical-to-optical conversion closer to the switch chip. Each switch has 18 removable external light sources, which supply light to the optical engines. Optical engines sit alongside the chip on the same package and convert electrical signals into light that carries data over fiber between parts of the cluster. Technicians can replace the light-source modules in the field, unlike traditional pluggable optics, which require replacing the entire module if a laser fails. Co-packaging shortens the electrical path from inches to millimeters, which reduces signal loss. It also removes the need for retimer chips, cutting both power draw and the number of parts in the signal path. In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. NVIDIA also ran the benchmark on 10,240 GPUs with GB300 systems, representing the largest scale in this round. Microsoft Azure matched that scale with 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 systems. Results at this scale matter because adding GPUs only speeds up training if they can work together efficiently. NVIDIA NVLink scale-up networking connects the GPUs within each system so they act as one, while NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet scale-out networking link those systems across the data center. Each of those steps generates tokens. Because AI data centers are limited by power, the more tokens a system can generate each second for every watt of power, the more agents it can serve and the more value it creates. articles.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology.   Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26   Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing workloads take a similar shape: an application reaches into an immense dataset, gathers a handful of scattered values, calculates a result and repeats this on an enormous scale. To help address the challenge, Rubin HPC will offer a balanced design, scaling data movement and compute together rather than increasing compute alone. That balance is what optimizes Rubin HPC for scientific computing. It keeps the GPU’s record number of CUDA cores supplied with data, so they spend their time computing rather than waiting. This accelerates recurring patterns of every simulation workload — from sparse matrix operations to stencil computations to sorting and reductions. These patterns are prevalent across data analytics, science and engineering workloads, which is why a purpose-built GPU delivering the broadest acceleration can help unlock cross-industry breakthroughs. NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries offer a growing set of optimized implementations of complex algorithms for agents to use, including those most relevant to simulation and analytics. Used together with Rubin HPC, the libraries can give agents the fastest glide path to reasoning outcomes. And faster agent-invoked simulations mean faster feedback — shortening the loop of hypothesis, simulation and refinement, so researchers and engineers can choose next steps sooner and point lab work at the most promising candidates. articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Vera CPU Platform to Accelerate Scientific Discovery
articles.summary: NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing — combining NVIDIA’s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for state-of-the-art scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science.
articles.fullText: News Summary: The NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform combines NVIDIA processors, NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking and breakthrough scientific software to boost weather, climate and molecular simulations. DKRZ has selected Vera CPUs for its HLRE-5 supercomputer for climate science. The full Vera CPU platform is coming from Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro. NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing — combining NVIDIA’s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for state-of-the-art scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science. The rack-scale platform brings together 192 Vera CPUs interconnected by NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking to meet the massive performance demands of climate modeling, molecular dynamics and other unaccelerated, next-generation scientific workloads. The liquid-cooled system delivers more than 200TB/s of aggregate peak memory bandwidth to support scientific simulation and AI workflows. “Scientific simulations need CPUs that can keep large datasets moving and sustain performance as applications scale,” said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Vera brings custom CPU cores, high-bandwidth memory and InfiniBand networking together to address those bottlenecks. With compilers and libraries optimized for Vera, researchers can run demanding simulations more efficiently and explore more complex scientific problems.” Engineered for Memory-Intensive HPC Each Vera CPU features 88 custom NVIDIA Olympus cores, 176 threads and compact, serviceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X memory delivering up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth to accelerate data-intensive scientific applications. The rack combines 192 Vera CPUs with approximately 300TB of memory and 1 petabyte of storage in a fully liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX™ design. Each 1U tray integrates eight Vera CPUs, and NVMe storage and management. The platform reuses NVL72 rack components, including chassis, power distribution and cooling infrastructure, to simplify deployment and service. NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking connects the system, and NVIDIA SHARP™ In-Network Computing helps scientists finish complex simulations faster by reducing the time processors spend coordinating their work. In NVIDIA’s tests, Vera delivered 1.9x the performance and 2.4x the performance per watt of x86 systems on OpenFOAM’s motorBike Large airflow simulation. Advancing Climate Science Research NVIDIA has benchmarked the open source Weather Research and Forecasting model on Vera CPUs, with projected performance gains of 1.6x and energy-efficiency gains of 2x compared with x86. DKRZ, the German Climate Computing Center, has selected Vera CPUs for its HLRE-5 supercomputer, alongside NVIDIA GB200 Grace Blackwell systems and NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking. Built by Bull and expected to be available in early 2028, the system will support climate simulation and AI research, enabling global kilometer-scale climate simulations with lower energy consumption than on the current system. Software and Availability To help researchers speed scientific applications, NVIDIA HPC SDK 26.11 is available now, providing compilers and libraries optimized for Vera. NVIDIA is also introducing a public beta of its next-generation Fortran compiler, which was built in collaboration with leading HPC centers and national labs. The new compiler gives developers a way to run their existing programs built on Fortran — the language that scientific computing was built on — with greater speed on NVIDIA platforms, without needing to rewrite their code. Vera CPU racks are expected to be available from Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro beginning in early 2027. Learn more about the NVIDIA Vera CPU . For detailed benchmark results and test configurations, read the NVIDIA Vera CPU HPC performance brief .

policyIdeas.title: 투자위축 대응형 구매확약·스케일업 보증
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 비R&D 금융·판로 사업으로 구매확약, 보증, 레퍼런스 확보를 묶어 민간 투자 공백을 완화
policyIdeas.why: AI·반도체 주가 변동성이 커지면 비상장 팹리스의 투자 유치와 고객 PoC가 동시에 지연될 수 있습니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 구매확약 금액, 보증 연계 금액, 후속 투자 유치, 고용 유지

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 수요연계 실증·구매전환 바우처
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 비R&D 성격으로 수요기관의 PoC 비용, 클라우드 전환비, 성능검증, 초기 구매비를 패키지로 지원
policyIdeas.why: 국내 NPU 기업은 기술개발 이후 레퍼런스, 구매사례, 운영검증이 부족해 매출 전환이 지연됩니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 유료 전환 PoC 수, 구매계약 금액, 국산 NPU 사용 시간, 고객 재구매율

policyIdeas.title: AI 서비스 기업·NPU 기업 매칭형 마켓플레이스
policyIdeas.budgetItem: AI 서비스·SaaS·SI 기업이 국산 NPU에서 모델을 시험하고 견적을 비교할 수 있는 중개 플랫폼 운영
policyIdeas.why: 비R&D 사업은 기술 자체보다 수요 발굴과 거래비용 절감이 중요합니다. 시장 접점을 만들면 기업 간 매칭 속도가 올라갑니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 등록 수요기업 수, 매칭 건수, PoC 전환율, 상용 계약 전환율

policyIdeas.title: 국산 AI컴퓨팅 성능·전력 검증 인증제
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 민간 시험기관과 연계해 추론 성능, 전력효율, 호환성, 보안성을 검증하고 인증마크를 부여
policyIdeas.why: 구매자는 칩 홍보자료보다 제3자 검증 데이터를 요구합니다. 인증 체계는 조달·금융·해외진출의 공통 근거가 됩니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 인증 제품 수, 공개 벤치마크 수, 조달 등록 건수, 인증 기반 계약 금액

policyIdeas.title: K-엔비디아 기업 공동 데모룸·상설 쇼케이스
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 5개 NPU 기업의 제품을 공공·민간 수요자가 직접 비교 체험할 수 있는 상설 데모룸과 온라인 쇼케이스 운영
policyIdeas.why: 비R&D 사업은 수요자가 실제 성능과 적용 시나리오를 이해하도록 만드는 접점이 중요합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 방문 수요기관 수, 데모 신청 건수, 후속 상담 건수, PoC 전환율

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 도입 컨설팅·전환 설계 지원단
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 수요기업의 기존 GPU 워크로드를 진단하고 국산 NPU 적용 가능성, 비용, 전력, 전환 일정을 설계해주는 컨설팅 지원
policyIdeas.why: 수요기업은 국산 NPU를 쓰고 싶어도 모델 변환, 운영비 비교, 리스크 판단을 자체적으로 하기 어렵습니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 전환진단 보고서 수, 전환 가능 워크로드 수, 실제 PoC 착수율, 예상 비용 절감액

policyIdeas.title: AI반도체 현장전문인력 전환 교육
policyIdeas.budgetItem: AI 서비스 개발자, MLOps 담당자, 공공 정보화 담당자를 대상으로 NPU 모델 최적화·운영 교육 제공
policyIdeas.why: 칩 도입은 하드웨어 구매만으로 끝나지 않고 운영인력이 있어야 반복 사용과 확산이 가능합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 교육 수료자 수, 기업별 적용 프로젝트 수, 모델 변환 성공률, 교육 후 PoC 착수율

policyIdeas.title: 온디바이스 AI 실증처 발굴 프로그램
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 제조, 보안, 모빌리티, 의료기기 분야에서 국산 NPU 모듈을 적용할 수요처를 발굴하고 실증 운영비 지원
policyIdeas.why: 데이터 외부 전송이 어렵거나 저전력이 중요한 분야는 국산 NPU가 차별화될 수 있는 초기 시장입니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 실증처 수, 제품 탑재 건수, 지연시간 개선, 전력 절감률

policyIdeas.title: 국산 NPU 기반 AI 데이터센터 전력절감 실증
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 공공·민간 데이터센터 일부 워크로드를 국산 NPU로 이전해 전력, 냉각, 비용 절감 효과를 검증
policyIdeas.why: AI 인프라 비용과 전력 문제가 커질수록 GPU 대체·보완재로서 국산 NPU의 정책 명분이 커집니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 전력 절감률, 랙당 처리량, 운영비 절감액, 전환 대상 워크로드 수

policyIdeas.title: 공공 AI서비스 국산 NPU 우선 실증 트랙
policyIdeas.budgetItem: 민원, 문서요약, 보안관제, 제조안전 등 공공 AI서비스에 국산 NPU 적용 가능성을 평가하는 운영비 지원
policyIdeas.why: 공공 부문은 초기 레퍼런스 시장을 열 수 있습니다. 단순 R&D 과제가 아니라 운영 워크로드 확보에 초점을 둬야 합니다.
policyIdeas.kpi: 공공 워크로드 수, 서비스 가동률, 비용 절감률, GPU 대비 전력 절감률

review.headline: 수출통제·AI컴퓨팅 안보, 파운드리·패키징 병목, AI 인프라 투자 신호를 중심으로, 신규 예산은 기술개발보다 수요 검증·운영 데이터·조달 전환을 강화하는 방향이 적절합니다.

sections.title: 정책수립 시사점
sections.body: 수출통제와 AI컴퓨팅 안보 신호가 강하면 국산 NPU 정책의 논리는 산업육성만이 아니라 안정적 조달과 국가 통제 가능한 AI 인프라 확보로 확장됩니다.
bullets: 해외 GPU 접근 리스크를 국산 AI컴퓨팅 도입 명분으로 정리
수출통제 대응 컨설팅과 조달 카탈로그를 함께 설계

sections.title: 시장·기술동향 판단
sections.body: AI 인프라 투자 확대와 공급망 재편은 국산 NPU에 기회지만, 실제 도입은 성능·전력·가격·운영 안정성 비교자료가 있어야 가능합니다.
bullets: 데이터센터 전력비와 추론비용 절감은 가장 설득력 있는 시장 진입 논리
온디바이스AI와 보안·금융 등 폐쇄망 수요는 해외 GPU 대비 차별화 가능성이 큼
파운드리·공급망 이슈는 국산 NPU 정책의 필요조건이지만, 구매전환을 보장하지는 않음

sections.title: 정부정책 방향
sections.body: 정부정책은 대체 컴퓨팅 확보와 보안검증을 묶어야 합니다. 단순 장비지원보다 공공기관이 실제로 사용할 수 있는 조달·보안·운영 기준을 만드는 것이 우선입니다.
bullets: 공공 폐쇄망 AI서비스 실증 트랙 신설
국산 NPU 보안성·공급 안정성 검증 리포트 발급
수출통제 리스크 진단과 대체 도입계획 컨설팅 지원

sections.title: 예산기획 체크포인트
sections.body: 우선 검토할 정책 아이템은 "투자위축 대응형 구매확약·스케일업 보증"입니다. 신규 예산은 제품 개발비보다 수요처 발굴, 실증 운영비, 성능검증, 구매전환 조건을 묶는 방향이 적합합니다.
bullets: 기업별 제품성숙도, 적용 가능 워크로드, 목표 수요처를 표준 양식으로 비교
시장 기사에서 반복되는 수요 분야를 공공 실증 후보 업무로 매핑
사업 공고에는 성능검증, 보안검증, 가격비교, 구매전환 조건을 필수 항목으로 포함
